# Kitchen Display Queue — 4h Implementation Plan

## Context
The repo is empty apart from `README.md` and the assessment PDF. We need an Express/Sequelize/Postgres API and a Vite/React/MUI web app. They're graded on layering, where the business rules live, and how well we can explain them. In the panel there will be a live change to **ranking or status rules**, so both rule sets have to be data-driven and live in one file each.

---

## 1) Deliverables checklist (+ companion tests)

**Infra / root**
- [ ] `docker-compose.yml`: postgres:16 only, `5433:5432`, user/pass/db = `kitchen_queue`
- [ ] Root `package.json` (npm workspaces `api`, `web`) with the scripts listed in §4
- [ ] `.nvmrc` (22), `engines.node >=22`, `.gitignore`
- [ ] `README.md`: prerequisites (Docker, Node 22), the 4 commands, ports (API 4000, web 5173), error-code table
- [ ] `DECISIONS.md`: Scope, Layers, Priority, Transitions, AI (one kept, one rejected, quoted), Next
- [ ] `ai-logs/`: export of the Claude Code transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/-Users-lui-rxredefined-test/*.jsonl`) plus this plan

**API (JS, Express, Sequelize 6, Jest)**
- [ ] Migrations: `menu_items`, `orders`, `order_items` (FKs, CHECKs, unique name, index on `orders.status`). No `sync()`
- [ ] Models for the 3 tables, with associations
- [ ] Seeder, with every date relative to `new Date()`, covering all 6 seed requirements in §9.5
- [ ] `GET /orders/queue[?status=received|preparing]`: sorted, each order has `score`
- [ ] `POST /orders/:id/{start,ready,pickup,cancel}`
- [ ] Error middleware returning `{ error: { code, message } }` with stable codes
- [ ] **Test `priority.test.js`** (pure, frozen `now`, no DB):
  - Example A = 60 and Example B = 60, with B ranked above A
  - Wait-time: 9m50s → 0, 10m → 5, cap at 40
  - Complexity: 14 → 0, 15 → 5, cap at 20
  - Promised: 20m → 25, exactly 30m → 25, 45m → 15, exactly 60m → 15, 61m → 0, null → 0, past → (our rule, see §5)
  - VIP +20, each type weight
  - Tie-breaks: promised_at (null last), then placed_at, then id
  - A delivery VIP with a tight promise beats a dine_in non-VIP
  - Score doesn't depend on `Date.now`: set fake system time to 1999 and get the same result
- [ ] **Test `transitions.test.js`** (pure): all 4 legal transitions pass. Rejected: skip (`received→ready`), repeat (`start` on `preparing`), from terminal (`picked_up`, `cancelled`), and `cancel` on `preparing`
- [ ] **Test `orders.api.test.js`** (supertest + test DB, frozen clock injected into `createApp`):
  - Each endpoint's happy path
  - 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`, 404 `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`, 400 `INVALID_ORDER_ID`, 400 `INVALID_STATUS_FILTER`
  - **cancelled, picked_up and ready orders are absent from the default queue**
  - Status filter works; the response order matches score order

**Web (Vite, React 19, TS, MUI 7)**
- [ ] One page with a dense MUI `Table` (size="small") showing score, customer, type, items summary, wait, promised, VIP chip, status
- [ ] Filter toggle: Active (default) / Received / Preparing, mapped to the query param
- [ ] One action button per row, taken from the API's `allowed_actions`, plus Cancel only when the API allows it
- [ ] Empty state; API errors shown in an MUI `Alert`/`Snackbar` with code and message; refetch after each action
- [ ] No scoring and no sorting on the client: rows render in the order the API returns them

## 2) Required vs optional vs out-of-scope

| Required | Optional (extra points, in priority order) | Out of scope |
|---|---|---|
| Everything in §1 | **a.** Vitest: Cancel shown only for `received` / empty state (~15 min) | Auth/roles, payments, customer entity |
| Pure priority fn + tests | **b.** `POST /orders` with validation + 1 Jest test (~30 min) | Pagination, Storybook, CI, design system |
| Server-enforced state machine + tests | **c.** Playwright e2e with `webServer` (~45 min, needs DB reset) | Redis, jobs, WebSockets, pixel-perfect |
| Migrations + relative seed | Polling the queue every ~30s so scores age on screen (5 min) | Menu CRUD |

## 3) Smallest repo structure
```
package.json  .nvmrc  docker-compose.yml  README.md  DECISIONS.md  ai-logs/
api/
  package.json  .sequelizerc  jest.config.js
  src/
    server.js                  # listen(4000)
    app.js                     # createApp({ clock }) → express, routes, error mw
    errors.js                  # AppError(code, status, message) + code constants
    endpoints/orders.js        # thin: parse req → call module → res.json
    modules/
      priority.js              # PURE. WEIGHTS/BUCKETS config, scoreOrder(order, now), compareRanked, rankQueue
      transitions.js           # PURE. ACTIONS = {start:{from:'received',to:'preparing'},...}, assertTransition, allowedActions(status)
      orders.js                # service: getQueue({status}, now), applyAction(id, action)
    repositories/orders.js     # findByStatuses(statuses) w/ items+menuItem, findById, updateStatusIfCurrent(id, from, to)
    schema/
      config.js                # DATABASE_URL, defaults to localhost:5433; test env → kitchen_queue_test
      models/{index,menu-item,order,order-item}.js
      migrations/  seeders/
  test/ priority.test.js  transitions.test.js  orders.api.test.js
web/
  package.json  vite.config.ts (proxy /orders → :4000)  tsconfig.json  index.html
  src/ main.tsx  App.tsx  api.ts (fetch + ApiError)  types.ts
       components/QueueTable.tsx  components/QueueFilter.tsx
```
Points to explain in the panel:
- Ranking change → edit only `priority.js`.
- Status change → edit `transitions.js`, plus a one-line migration if a new status value is added.
- The UI doesn't know any transition rules because the API sends `allowed_actions`.

## 4) Root scripts
```jsonc
"workspaces": ["api", "web"],
"scripts": {
  "db:setup": "npm run db:setup -w api",   // sequelize db:migrate && db:seed:all (seeder clears its tables first → idempotent)
  "db:reset": "npm run db:reset -w api",   // migrate:undo:all && db:setup (fresh relative dates before a demo)
  "dev": "concurrently -n api,web \"npm run dev -w api\" \"npm run dev -w web\"",  // api: node --watch src/server.js
  "test": "npm test -w api && npm test -w web --if-present",
  "test:api": "npm test -w api",           // api pretest: NODE_ENV=test sequelize db:create (ignore exists) + db:migrate
  "test:web": "npm test -w web",
  "test:e2e": "npm run test:e2e -w web"    // only if extra (c) is done
}
```
Install is plain `npm install` at the root. Root devDep: `concurrently`. API deps: express, sequelize, pg, sequelize-cli, jest, supertest. Web: the Vite react-ts template plus @mui/material, @emotion/*, and later vitest + @testing-library/react.

## 5) Ambiguous rules → proposed interpretation (each one goes in DECISIONS.md)
1. **Promised bucket boundaries.** The spec says "within 30" and "31–60", which leaves 30–31 min (e.g. 30m30s) undefined. Use ms-precise `minutesUntil ≤ 30 → 25`, `≤ 60 → 15`, otherwise 0. Exactly 30 and exactly 60 are both inclusive.
2. **Overdue `promised_at`** (in the past). Score it 25, the most urgent bucket. Ignoring it and scoring 0 would sink late orders, which is the wrong product behaviour.
3. **`promised_at` on dine_in.** The spec says it's "relevant for delivery and takeout". Scoring stays generic, so any `promised_at` counts. The seed and `POST /orders` reject `promised_at` on dine_in. Alternative to flag: ignore it in scoring for dine_in.
4. **`placed_at` in the future** (clock skew). Clamp `minutes_waiting` to ≥ 0.
5. **Rounding.** Wait time uses floor of whole minutes. `total_prep` is an integer sum. Score is always an integer.
6. **Cancel is only allowed from `received`.** Cancelling a `preparing` order returns 409, as the spec says.
7. **Repeated or concurrent transitions.** Use a conditional `UPDATE … WHERE id=? AND status=from`. If 0 rows change, re-read the order: missing → 404, otherwise 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION` with `{current_status, action}`. This also handles two expeditors double-clicking at once.
8. **Invalid `?status=`** (e.g. `ready`, `foo`). Return 400 `INVALID_STATUS_FILTER` rather than silently falling back to the default.
9. **HTTP statuses.** 404 not found, 409 illegal transition, 400 malformed id/filter/body, 422 (or 400) unknown `menu_item_id` on POST /orders.
10. **Seed tie that stays stable.** Scores drift as wall-clock time passes. Give the tied pair the same type, VIP flag, items and `placed_at`, with both `promised_at` values > 60 min away (e.g. +2h and +3h). They then tie for about an hour and promised_at decides the order. Caps: one order placed ~3h ago (wait = 40) and one with ≥ 60 prep minutes (complexity = 20).
11. **Where wait minutes come from.** The API returns `minutes_waiting` computed with the same `now` as the score, so the UI does no time math beyond formatting.

## 6) Implementation sequence (~240 min, commit at each checkpoint with your OK)
| # | Time | Step | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0:00–0:20 | Scaffold: root workspaces, compose, api skeleton, `npm create vite` web, MUI install | `docker compose up -d`, `npm install` and `npm run dev` all boot |
| 1 | 0:20–0:50 | `priority.js` written test-first from Examples A/B, then caps, buckets, tie-break | priority tests green, no DB |
| 2 | 0:50–1:05 | `transitions.js` + tests | pure transition tests green |
| 3 | 1:05–1:45 | Migrations, models, relative seed, `db:setup` | `npm run db:setup` is idempotent and the seed covers all of §9.5 |
| 4 | 1:45–2:25 | Repository → service → endpoints → error mw; `createApp({clock})`; api integration tests | curl + supertest green |
| 5 | 2:25–3:15 | Web: api client, table, filter, actions, error Alert, empty state | manual run against the seed |
| 6 | 3:15–3:35 | Extra (a) Vitest; extra (b) POST /orders only if ahead of schedule | — |
| 7 | 3:35–3:55 | README, DECISIONS, ai-logs export, clean-clone smoke test (`git clone` → 4 commands) | everything boots from a fresh clone |
| 8 | 3:55–4:00 | Buffer | — |

## 7) Deliberate cuts
- **Playwright e2e (extra c).** Highest cost and flakiest, because it needs DB reset and orchestration of two servers. Listed as skipped in DECISIONS.
- **POST /orders (extra b).** Done only if step 5 finishes before 3:15.
- **Out of scope / not built:** menu endpoints, any create-order UI, pagination, real-time updates (at most a 30s poll), DB-level ENUM types (VARCHAR + CHECK is easier to change live), a validation library (hand-rolled checks are enough), state management or router libraries in web, Docker for the apps, and styling polish beyond a dense MUI table.

## Verification
- `npm run test:api`: priority and transition suites run without Postgres, then the integration suite runs against `kitchen_queue_test`.
- `docker compose up -d && npm install && npm run db:setup && npm run dev`, then open :5173. Check that:
  - the tie pair is ordered by promised_at;
  - capped orders are visible;
  - the ready order is absent;
  - start/ready/cancel work;
  - a forced illegal call (`curl -X POST :4000/orders/<preparing-id>/start`) returns 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`.
- Final step: fresh-clone smoke test.

entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

Install is plain `npm install` at the root. Root devDep: `concurrently`. API deps: express, sequelize, pg, sequelize-cli, jest, supertest. Web: the Vite react-ts template plus @mui/material, @emotion/*, and later vitest + @testing-library/react.

## 5) Ambiguous rules → proposed interpretation (each one goes in DECISIONS.md)
1. **Promised bucket boundaries.** The spec says "within 30" and "31–60", which leaves 30–31 min (e.g. 30m30s) undefined. Use ms-precise `minutesUntil ≤ 30 → 25`, `≤ 60 → 15`, otherwise 0. Exactly 30 and exactly 60 are both inclusive.
2. **Overdue `promised_at`** (in the past). Score it 25, the most urgent bucket. Ignoring it and scoring 0 would sink late orders, which is the wrong product behaviour.
3. **`promised_at` on dine_in.** The spec says it's "relevant for delivery and takeout". Scoring stays generic, so any `promised_at` counts. The seed and `POST /orders` reject `promised_at` on dine_in. Alternative to flag: ignore it in scoring for dine_in.
4. **`placed_at` in the future** (clock skew). Clamp `minutes_waiting` to ≥ 0.
5. **Rounding.** Wait time uses floor of whole minutes. `total_prep` is an integer sum. Score is always an integer.
6. **Cancel is only allowed from `received`.** Cancelling a `preparing` order returns 409, as the spec says.
7. **Repeated or concurrent transitions.** Use a conditional `UPDATE … WHERE id=? AND status=from`. If 0 rows change, re-read the order: missing → 404, otherwise 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION` with `{current_status, action}`. This also handles two expeditors double-clicking at once.
8. **Invalid `?status=`** (e.g. `ready`, `foo`). Return 400 `INVALID_STATUS_FILTER` rather than silently falling back to the default.
9. **HTTP statuses.** 404 not found, 409 illegal transition, 400 malformed id/filter/body, 422 (or 400) unknown `menu_item_id` on POST /orders.
10. **Seed tie that stays stable.** Scores drift as wall-clock time passes. Give the tied pair the same type, VIP flag, items and `placed_at`, with both `promised_at` values > 60 min away (e.g. +2h and +3h). They then tie for about an hour and promised_at decides the order. Caps: one order placed ~3h ago (wait = 40) and one with ≥ 60 prep minutes (complexity = 20).
11. **Where wait minutes come from.** The API returns `minutes_waiting` computed with the same `now` as the score, so the UI does no time math beyond formatting.

## 6) Implementation sequence (~240 min, commit at each checkpoint with your OK)
| # | Time | Step | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0:00–0:20 | Scaffold: root workspaces, compose, api skeleton, `npm create vite` web, MUI install | `docker compose up -d`, `npm install` and `npm run dev` all boot |
| 1 | 0:20–0:50 | `priority.js` written test-first from Examples A/B, then caps, buckets, tie-break | priority tests green, no DB |
| 2 | 0:50–1:05 | `transitions.js` + tests | pure transition tests green |
| 3 | 1:05–1:45 | Migrations, models, relative seed, `db:setup` | `npm run db:setup` is idempotent and the seed covers all of §9.5 |
| 4 | 1:45–2:25 | Repository → service → endpoints → error mw; `createApp({clock})`; api integration tests | curl + supertest green |
| 5 | 2:25–3:15 | Web: api client, table, filter, actions, error Alert, empty state | manual run against the seed |
| 6 | 3:15–3:35 | Extra (a) Vitest; extra (b) POST /orders only if ahead of schedule | — |
| 7 | 3:35–3:55 | README, DECISIONS, ai-logs export, clean-clone smoke test (`git clone` → 4 commands) | everything boots from a fresh clone |
| 8 | 3:55–4:00 | Buffer | — |

## 7) Deliberate cuts
- **Playwright e2e (extra c).** Highest cost and flakiest, because it needs DB reset and orchestration of two servers. Listed as skipped in DECISIONS.
- **POST /orders (extra b).** Done only if step 5 finishes before 3:15.
- **Out of scope / not built:** menu endpoints, any create-order UI, pagination, real-time updates (at most a 30s poll), DB-level ENUM types (VARCHAR + CHECK is easier to change live), a validation library (hand-rolled checks are enough), state management or router libraries in web, Docker for the apps, and styling polish beyond a dense MUI table.

## Verification
- `npm run test:api`: priority and transition suites run without Postgres, then the integration suite runs against `kitchen_queue_test`.
- `docker compose up -d && npm install && npm run db:setup && npm run dev`, then open :5173. Check that:
  - the tie pair is ordered by promised_at;
  - capped orders are visible;
  - the ready order is absent;
  - start/ready/cancel work;
  - a forced illegal call (`curl -X POST :4000/orders/<preparing-id>/start`) returns 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`.
- Final step: fresh-clone smoke test.

content.text:
The scaffold is in place and installs, type-checks, builds and boots under Node 22. I couldn't check Postgres because Docker Desktop isn't running on your machine. Nothing is committed yet.

**What I created**
- **Root:** `package.json` sets up the npm workspaces (`api`, `web`) and has `dev`, `build` and `test` scripts; `dev` starts both apps together. Also `package-lock.json`, `.gitignore`, and `docker-compose.yml`, copied exactly from the spec (Postgres 16 on port 5433).
- **Node 22 enforcement:** `.nvmrc` says `22`, every `package.json` requires Node `>=22 <23`, and `.npmrc` sets `engine-strict=true` so npm refuses to install on any other version.
- **`api/`** (CommonJS):
  - `src/app.js` exports `createApp()`, an Express app that only parses JSON and has no routes yet.
  - `src/server.js` listens on port 4000 (or `PORT`).
  - Installed now so later steps don't need installs: express 5.2.1, sequelize 6.37.8, pg, sequelize-cli, jest 30, supertest.
- **`web/`**: Vite 8.3, React 19.3, MUI 7.3.11, TypeScript 5.9 in strict mode.
  - `main.tsx` sets up the MUI theme and base styles.
  - `App.tsx` is only the page heading "Kitchen Display", which is where the queue page will go.
  - Vite forwards `/orders` requests to port 4000, so the web app needs no CORS setup.
  - There are no demo assets, logos or default Vite CSS.

**Check results**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm install` (Node 22.15.0) | ✅ 593 packages |
| Installs refused on Node 24 | ✅ fails with `EBADENGINE` |
| `npm run build` (type-check, then Vite build) | ✅ |
| `npm test` (Jest) | ✅ exits 0 with no tests yet; it currently allows an empty test run |
| API starts | ✅ listens and returns 404, as expected with no routes |
| Web dev server starts | ✅ page title loads and `main.tsx` returns 200 |
| `docker compose config` | ✅ valid |
| `docker compose up -d` | ❌ not run: Docker isn't running |

**Things to know**
- Your shell defaults to Node 24, which will now fail on install. Run `nvm use` in the repo first; I ran all checks with Node 22 explicitly.
- `npm audit` reports 2 moderate issues, both from `uuid@8` pulled in by sequelize 6. The only fix it offers is a forced breaking change, so I left it.
- I pinned MUI to `^7` and TypeScript to `~5.9`, although MUI 9 and TypeScript 7 are the latest releases. The spec requires MUI 7, and TypeScript 7 is the new native compiler, which I didn't want to risk. Express is v5.
- There's no `db:setup` script yet because there are no migrations. It gets added with the schema step.

Next steps:
- Start Docker Desktop so we can check Postgres.
- Tell me whether to commit, and whether to commit or ignore the assessment PDF (it's still untracked).

file.content:
# Decisions

- [ ] **No `concurrently` lib install for local dev commands: The assessment explicity asks to **not use external libraries**, so a simpler command `npm run dev -w api & npm run dev -w web` was chosen aware of the trade-offs.
- [ ] **Bucket boundaries**: Treat the 0-30 and 31-60 as both inclusive on the right side of the interval so there is no gaps between them. Use ms-precise `minutesUntil ≤ 30 → 25`, `≤ 60 → 15`, otherwise 0. Exactly 30 and exactly 60 are both inclusive.
- [ ] **Overdue `promised_at`**: If timestamp is in the past, score it 25, the most urgent bucket.
- [ ] **`promised_at` on dine_in.** The spec says it's "relevant for delivery and takeout", so we are ignoring it for dine_in.
- [ ] **`placed_at` in the future** (clock skew): Clamp `minutes_waiting` to ≥ 0.
- [ ] **Rounding.** Wait time uses floor of whole minutes, `total_prep` is always an integer sum.
- [ ] **Explicit state machine**: No conditionals should be scattered throughout the code. The module receives the current status and the next and rejects everything not in the map. Endpoints `/start`, `/ready`, `/pickup` e `/cancel` can only map the action to its corresponding destination status.
```
const ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS = {
  received: ["preparing", "cancelled"],
  preparing: ["ready"],
  ready: ["picked_up"],
  picked_up: [],
  cancelled: [],
};
```
- [ ] **Cancel is only allowed from `received`.** Cancelling a `preparing` order returns 409, as the spec says.
- [ ] **Invalid `?status=`** (e.g. `ready`, `foo`). Return 400 `INVALID_STATUS_FILTER` rather than silently falling back to the default.
- [ ] **HTTP statuses.** 404 not found, 409 illegal transition, 400 malformed id/filter/body, 422 (or 400) unknown `menu_item_id` on POST /orders.
- [ ] **Seed tie that stays stable.** Scores drift as wall-clock time passes.
- [ ] **Where wait minutes come from API.** Return a `minutes_waiting` field that is alreadycomputed with the same `now` as the score, so the UI does no time math beyond formatting.

content.text:
I've added `api/src/modules/priority.js` with tests in `api/test/priority.test.js`, and all 39 tests pass with `npm test -w api`. Postgres isn't involved: the module imports nothing and never reads the system clock.

**How `priority.js` is laid out**
- **All ranking numbers sit in one `PRIORITY_RULES` object:** type points, VIP points, the wait-time and complexity steps and caps, the promise buckets, and which order types a promise counts for. A ranking change in the panel should mostly mean editing that object and its tests.
- **What it exports:**
  - `scoreOrder(order, now)` returns the number the spec asks for.
  - `scoreBreakdown(order, now)` returns the points for each part plus the total. It's useful for explaining a score.
  - `compareByPriority` sorts by score, then `promised_at` (no promise last), then `placed_at`, then `id`.
  - `rankOrders(orders, now)` returns new, sorted objects carrying `score` and `minutes_waiting`, both computed with the same `now`. It doesn't change its input.
- **Input:** a plain object `{ id, type, is_vip, placed_at, promised_at, items: [{ quantity, prep_time_minutes }] }`. Turning database rows into this shape will be the repository's job. Timestamps can be `Date` objects or ISO strings.
- **It throws instead of returning a bad score** when `type` is unknown or a timestamp is invalid, so a broken order can't quietly score `NaN`.

**Your DECISIONS rules as implemented**
- **Bucket boundaries:** exactly 30 and exactly 60 minutes are included in their buckets, and the check uses fractional minutes, so 30m30s gets 15 points.
- **Overdue promise:** gets 25 points.
- **Future `placed_at`:** waiting time is clamped to 0.
- **Dine-in promise:** ignored. One step past what DECISIONS currently says: it's ignored in the tie-break as well as the score, through one shared helper. Otherwise a dine-in promise would add 0 points but still jump ahead in a tie. Please add that line to DECISIONS.

**What the tests cover**
- Examples A and B each score 60 with the exact per-part breakdown, and B ranks above A.
- Each type's points, and the VIP bonus.
- Wait time at 9m50s, 10m, 79m and 80m+, and the future clamp.
- Complexity at 14, 15, the 50-minute example and the cap.
- Every promise bucket, its edges, overdue and null, and takeout versus dine-in.
- Each tie-break level, and the case where a delivery VIP with a tight promise beats a dine-in non-VIP.
- Changing the system clock doesn't change the score.

**Two things I noticed in your edits**
1. **The DECISIONS entry about `concurrently`** says the assessment "explicitly asks to not use external libraries", but it doesn't. Section 9 only says "Do not depend on any private or external repository", which is about git repos, not npm packages. The panel reads DECISIONS first, so I'd reword the reason to something like "kept dependencies minimal".
2. **The root `dev` script.**
   - It currently has `&&`, so the API watcher never exits and the web app never starts.
   - Switching to `&` fixes that, but the backgrounded API keeps running after Ctrl-C and holds port 4000.
   - If that bothers you, a ~10-line `scripts/dev.js` that starts both and stops both together would fix it without adding a library.

# Decisions

- [ ] **JS API requirement is enriched with JSDoc typings and ts-check annotations.**
- [ ] **Bucket boundaries**: Treat the 0-30 and 31-60 as both inclusive on the right side of the interval so there is no gaps between them. Use ms-precise `minutesUntil ≤ 30 → 25`, `≤ 60 → 15`, otherwise 0. Exactly 30 and exactly 60 are both inclusive.
- [ ] **Overdue `promised_at`**: If timestamp is in the past, score it 25, the most urgent bucket.
- [ ] **`promised_at` on dine_in.** The spec says it's "relevant for delivery and takeout", so we are ignoring it for dine_in.
- [ ] **`placed_at` in the future** (clock skew): Clamp `minutes_waiting` to ≥ 0.
- [ ] **Rounding.** Wait time uses floor of whole minutes, `total_prep` is always an integer sum.
- [ ] **Explicit state machine**: No conditionals should be scattered throughout the code. The module receives the current status and the next and rejects everything not in the map. Endpoints `/start`, `/ready`, `/pickup` e `/cancel` can only map the action to its corresponding destination status.
```
const ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS = {
  received: ["preparing", "cancelled"],
  preparing: ["ready"],
  ready: ["picked_up"],
  picked_up: [],
  cancelled: [],
};
```
- [ ] **Cancel is only allowed from `received`.** Cancelling a `preparing` order returns 409, as the spec says.
- [ ] **Invalid `?status=`** (e.g. `ready`, `foo`). Return 400 `INVALID_STATUS_FILTER` rather than silently falling back to the default.
- [ ] **HTTP statuses.** 404 not found, 409 illegal transition, 400 malformed id/filter/body, 422 (or 400) unknown `menu_item_id` on POST /orders.
- [ ] **Seed tie that stays stable.** Scores drift as wall-clock time passes.
- [ ] **Where wait minutes come from API.** Return a `minutes_waiting` field that is alreadycomputed with the same `now` as the score, so the UI does no time math beyond formatting.  "scripts": {

    "build": "npm run build -w web",

content.text:
I've written the state machine in `api/src/modules/transitions.js`, with 41 tests in `api/test/transitions.test.js`. All 80 API tests pass and the new files type-check clean under `// @ts-check`. I've also saved a memory note so every new API file gets `// @ts-check` and JSDoc types.

**What I added:**
- **`transitions.js`**
  - **`ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS`** is your map exactly as written in DECISIONS, frozen so nothing can change it at runtime. It's the only place the rules live.
  - **`ACTION_TARGET_STATUS`** maps each endpoint action to the status it moves to (`start` → `preparing`, `ready` → `ready`, `pickup` → `picked_up`, `cancel` → `cancelled`). It says nothing about which statuses an action is allowed from; only the map decides that. This matches your DECISIONS rule that endpoints only map an action to its destination.
  - **`canTransition(from, to)`** is one lookup in the map, with no special cases. That single check rejects skipped steps, repeating the current status, leaving a terminal status, and unknown statuses. It also rejects tricks like a status called `constructor`.
  - **`assertTransition(from, to)`** returns the new status, or throws `INVALID_TRANSITION` with `{ from, to }` attached. So starting an order that is already `preparing` fails with `INVALID_TRANSITION` rather than succeeding silently.
  - **`allowedActions(status)`** is worked out from the two maps, e.g. `received` → `['start', 'cancel']`, `picked_up` → `[]`. The API can send this with each order so the UI shows the right buttons without its own copy of the rules.
  - **`ORDER_STATUSES`** is the list of statuses, taken from the map's keys. The schema step can reuse it for the database check on the status column.
- **`api/src/errors.js`** is new: a small `DomainError` class with a fixed `code` and extra details. Turning codes into HTTP statuses (409 for this one) is left to the endpoint layer.

**What the tests cover:**
- Each of the 4 legal transitions succeeds, and they are the only legal ones out of all 25 status pairs.
- Rejected: skipped steps, repeating every status, every move out of `picked_up` and `cancelled`, moving backwards, cancelling a `preparing` order, and unknown statuses.
- The error carries its code and the attempted `from` and `to`.

content.text:
`npm run db:setup` now works and can be run any number of times. A second run skips the migrations, then the seed clears the tables and inserts the same 12 menu items, 10 orders and 15 order items with the same ids. I checked this against the running Postgres. All 80 tests still pass and every new file type-checks under `// @ts-check`.

**Scripts:**
- In `api/`: `db:migrate`, `db:seed`, and `db:setup`, which runs one then the other.
- At the root: `npm run db:setup` calls the API one.
- Migrations are tracked in Postgres, so a rerun skips them. Seeds are not tracked by default, so the seed runs every time and clears the tables first.

**Schema files** (all under `api/src/schema/`, with `api/.sequelizerc` pointing the CLI there):
- **`config.js`**: connection settings, defaulting to the docker-compose database on port 5433. `DATABASE_URL` overrides them, and timestamps are stored in UTC.
- **Three migrations**, one each for `menu_items`, `orders` and `order_items`:
  - **Checks:** names can't be blank, and type, status and category must be valid values. Prep time and quantity must be positive.
  - **Uniqueness and links:** menu item names are unique. Order items must point at a real order and menu item; deleting an order deletes its items, and a menu item that's in use can't be deleted.
  - **Indexes:** on `orders.status` and `order_items.order_id`.
  - The allowed values are written out in each migration rather than imported from the modules, so a later change to the app can't silently rewrite schema history.
- **`models/index.js`**: the connection and the three models, linked so an order has `items` and each item has its `menu_item`. It contains no queries and never calls `sync()`.
- **The seeder**:
  - It clears the three tables and restarts their ids inside a transaction, then inserts everything.
  - All dates are worked out from the moment it runs.
  - It looks up menu items by name and fails loudly if an order uses a name that isn't on the menu.

**Seed vs the spec**, checked by running the seeded orders through `rankOrders`:

| Score | Order | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| 75 | Bruno, dine_in VIP, preparing | complexity cap (72 prep min) |
| 70 | Ana, dine_in, placed 3h ago | wait-time cap |
| 65 | Gabi, takeout, promise 10 min overdue | overdue promise scores 25 |
| 55 | Elena, delivery VIP, promised in 20 min | VIP plus a tight promise |
| 45 | Felipe, delivery, promised in 45 min | the 31–60 minute bucket |
| 20 / 20 | Carla (promised in 2h) above Diego (promised in 3h) | tie broken by `promised_at` |
| none | Hugo `ready`, Iris `picked_up`, João `cancelled` | statuses outside the active queue |

- **The tie only shows `promised_at` at work.** Carla and Diego share `placed_at`, and Diego has the lower id, so nothing but the promise can put Carla first.
- **It stays visible for about an hour after seeding.** Both promises are over an hour away and score 0. After that Carla's promise starts adding points, so she stays ahead.

**Database checks:**
- Undoing all migrations and running `db:setup` again works cleanly.
- Postgres rejected every bad insert I tried: a blank name, an unknown type or status, a zero quantity, a missing order, a duplicate menu name, and deleting a menu item that's in use.

**One workaround:** Sequelize's type definitions leave out the `returning` option on `bulkInsert`, although Postgres supports it at runtime. I wrapped those options in a small `insertReturning` helper with a comment, rather than turning type-checking off.

content.text:
Integration tests now run against their own database, `kitchen_queue_test`, on the same Postgres. A separate script creates it, and Jest only checks it's ready. All 88 tests pass and the new checked files type-check clean.

**New scripts**
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run db:test:setup` | Drops `kitchen_queue_test`, recreates it and runs all migrations, so you always start from a fresh copy of the current schema |
| `npm test` | Runs unit and integration tests together, one test file at a time |
| `npm run test:unit` | Pure module tests only; no Postgres needed |
| `npm run test:integration` | Postgres tests only |

**Files**
- **`api/src/schema/config.js`**: adds a `test` setting with its own database. It defaults to `kitchen_queue_test` on port 5433, and `TEST_DATABASE_URL` overrides it. Jest sets `NODE_ENV=test`, which makes the models use it.
- **`api/jest.config.js`**: splits tests into two groups:
  - `unit` runs `test/*.test.js` and has no database setup.
  - `integration` runs `test/integration/**/*.test.js`.
- **`test/integration/global-setup.js`**: only checks; it never creates or migrates anything. If the test database is missing or has migrations not yet applied, Jest stops straight away. I tested this before creating the database; it printed:
  > Integration test database is not ready (database "kitchen_queue_test" does not exist). Run `npm run db:test:setup` (with `docker compose up -d`) first.
- **`test/integration/helpers/db.js`**:
  - `resetDb()` empties the tables and restarts ids before each test. It refuses to run unless the database name ends in `_test`, so it can never wipe the demo data.
  - `createMenuItem` and `createOrder` insert small test rows; tests never use the demo seed.
  - `closeDb()` closes the connection when a file's tests finish.
- **`test/integration/schema.test.js`** (8 tests) proves the setup end to end:
  - an order and its items load back together;
  - timestamps come back in UTC;
  - the database itself rejects a blank name, an unknown type or status, a zero quantity, and a menu item that doesn't exist;
  - deleting an order deletes its items.

Running `db:test:setup` a second time rebuilt the test database cleanly. The demo database still has its 10 seeded orders.

The repository tests come next and will use the same helpers. They'll include the outstanding one: cancelled and picked-up orders never appear in the default queue.

content.text:
The API side is complete: repository, service, endpoints and error handling, all wired through `createApp({ clock })`. All 119 tests pass (82 unit, 37 integration), the integration suite passed 5 runs in a row, and every new file type-checks under `// @ts-check`. I also ran the real server against the seeded database with curl and it returned the expected ranking.

**The layers**
| Layer | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoint | `src/endpoints/orders.js` | Checks the `:id` is a positive integer, calls the service and returns JSON. The four action routes are written out explicitly. No business rules. |
| Error handling | `src/endpoints/errors.js` | Turns error codes into HTTP statuses, in one place. Every error response looks like `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`. |
| Module | `src/modules/orders.js` | `getQueue` checks the status filter, loads orders, ranks them and adds `allowed_actions`. `applyAction` loads the order, checks the transition, then updates. Defines the active queue as `received` and `preparing`. |
| Repository | `src/repositories/orders.js` | `findByStatuses`, `findById`, `updateStatusIfCurrent`. It returns plain objects, so no Sequelize objects reach the module. Items come back in a stable order. |
| App | `src/app.js` | `createApp({ clock, ordersService })` defaults to the real clock; tests pass a frozen one. |

**Two concurrent clicks on the same order**
- The update only applies if the order is still in the status that was checked. If someone else changed it first, the request gets 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION` naming the current status.
- If the order disappeared in between, it gets `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`.
- A test fires two simultaneous `start` requests and always gets one 200 and one 409.

**Error codes**, ready to copy into the README:
| Code | HTTP | When |
|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_ORDER_ID` | 400 | `:id` isn't a positive 32-bit integer |
| `INVALID_STATUS_FILTER` | 400 | `?status=` is anything except `received` or `preparing` (including repeated) |
| `INVALID_JSON` | 400 | The request body isn't valid JSON |
| `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No order with that id |
| `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown path or action |
| `INVALID_TRANSITION` | 409 | The state machine rejects the change, or another request changed the status first |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Anything unexpected (the error is logged on the server) |

**What the integration tests cover**
- **Queue ranking:** spec Examples A and B, run through HTTP with the frozen clock, come back as B then A with score 60 each. A check of A's full response shape is included.
- **Active queue membership:** `ready`, `picked_up` and `cancelled` orders are left out. An order that is cancelled or picked up through the API leaves the queue; this is the transition test the spec asked for.
- **Filtering:** both valid filters work, four invalid ones return 400, and an empty queue returns `{ orders: [] }`.
- **Actions:** each legal action works and is saved. Six illegal cases return 409 and leave the status unchanged: a repeat, two skipped steps, cancelling a `preparing` order, and two from a terminal status.
- **Errors:** an unknown order returns 404, malformed ids return 400, plus the unknown-route and bad-JSON cases.

**Things to know**
- **New dev dependency:** `@types/express` on the API, so Express code type-checks; without it every request handler was untyped.
- **Action response shape:** the action endpoints return `{ order }` with the new status and `allowed_actions`, but no `score`, since the score is only meaningful within the queue. The UI will just refetch the queue after each action.
- **`DomainError` naming:** endpoints also throw `DomainError` for `INVALID_ORDER_ID`, so the name is now slightly too narrow. Renaming it to `AppError` is a small rename if you want it.
- **Nothing is committed yet.** I reset the demo data after the curl test.

The web UI is next on the plan.

content.text:
A dine_in promise now counts in the tie-break but still earns no points, and all 119 tests pass.

**The split in `priority.js`**
- **`scorablePromisedAt(order)`** is used only when scoring. It returns the promise for types in `PRIORITY_RULES.promised.appliesTo` (takeout, delivery), so a dine_in promise still scores 0.
- **`tieBreakPromisedAt(order)`** is used only by `compareByPriority`. It returns any non-null `promised_at`, whatever the order type.
- `scorablePromisedAt` first checks the type, then hands off to `tieBreakPromisedAt`, so both read the timestamp the same way.
- I updated the comments to match.

**Tests in `priority.test.js`**
- **Replaced:** "dine_in promised_at is ignored in the tie-break" became "dine_in promised_at scores nothing but wins the tie-break over a null promise". The promised order is placed later and has the higher id, so only the promise can put it first. Both orders score 30.
- **New:** two tied dine_in orders that both have promises put the earlier promise first.
- **Updated, and it now flips:** in the tie across types, a dine_in promised in 30 min beats a takeout promised in 120 min, both on 30 points.
- **Removed:** my earlier test expecting `placed_at` to decide between two tied dine_in orders, since it encoded the rule you just changed.
- **Unchanged:** the scoring test that a dine_in promise adds 0 points.

When I switched the tie-break back to the old helper, these three tests failed and the rest passed, so they pin the new rule.

The cross-type case follows from comparing promises regardless of type: a tied dine_in with an earlier promise now beats a takeout or delivery order with a later one. If you meant dine_in promises to win only against orders with no promise, tell me and I'll change it.

Two loose ends:
- **DECISIONS:** the `promised_at` on dine_in line still says it's ignored. It could read: "Scores 0 points (the spec scores promises only for delivery and takeout), but a dine_in promise still counts in the tie-break, ahead of orders with no promise."
- **Seed:** there's no dine_in order with a promise, so the demo can't show this rule.
Let's append those two loose ends changes while I review the latest API changes.

content.text:
The Kitchen Display page is built, type-checks, and works against your running servers: the queue, actions, error banner, filter and empty state all behave as the spec asks. I clicked through it in a real browser. Nothing is committed.

**Files in `web/src/`**
| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `types.ts` | Mirrors the API response shapes: order type, status, action, and the queue order with `score`, `minutes_waiting` and `allowed_actions`. |
| `api.ts` | `fetchQueue(filter)` and `applyOrderAction(id, action)`. Any failure becomes an `ApiError` with a code and message. If the API is down, that's `NETWORK_ERROR`. |
| `useQueue.ts` | Loads the queue for the current filter and cancels an older request when a newer one starts. `runAction` reloads after every action, success or not, so the screen catches up if it was stale. |
| `components/QueueFilterToggle.tsx` | Active queue / Received / Preparing. |
| `components/QueueTable.tsx` | Compact MUI table with score, customer #id, type, items, waiting, promised time, VIP chip, status chip and action buttons. Shows "No orders in the queue." when empty. |
| `App.tsx` | Header with the filter and a Refresh button, the error banner, a loading bar, and the table. |

**No business rules on the client**
- Scores, sort order and `minutes_waiting` come from the API as-is, and rows render in the order received.
- The buttons come from each order's `allowed_actions`; the UI only maps action names to labels.
- The only time handling is showing the promised time in local time.

**Checked in the browser**
- **Queue:** the seeded queue renders in API order, with both ties: Lucas above Karin, and Carla above Diego. No console warnings.
- **Start on Ana:** her row changed to `preparing` and now shows only Ready.
- **Rejected action:** I started Karin through the API, then clicked her now-stale Cancel button. A red banner showed `INVALID_TRANSITION: Cannot change order status from 'preparing' to 'cancelled'`, and the table reloaded with her real status.
- **Received filter:** showed only the 4 received orders, still in API order.
- **Empty state:** I emptied that view in the dev database and pressed Refresh; the empty-state message appeared.

**One fix from the browser check:** the error banner stayed up after switching filters, which was misleading. It's now cleared when the filter changes; after the fix, the banner was gone on switching back.

**Cleanup**
- I reseeded the demo database.
- I deleted the `.playwright-mcp/` folder the browser tool wrote into the repo.
- I only stopped my own duplicate `npm run dev` (it failed because your servers already held the ports); yours are still running.

**Left as is**
- Column widths shift slightly between a full and an empty table.
- The queue doesn't refresh on its own: scores and waiting times only update on Refresh or after an action. A 30-second automatic refresh would be about 5 lines if you want it.

content.text:
I fixed both review points; the build passes, and in the browser the filter and Refresh are now disabled while an action runs.

**Should fix: filter out of sync with the table**
- **`QueueFilterToggle`** now takes an optional `disabled` prop, which it passes to the toggle group.
- **`App.tsx`** sets `actionPending = pendingOrderId !== null`. That disables the filter, and Refresh is disabled when `loading || actionPending`.
- **`useQueue.ts` needed a change too.** `runAction` was clearing `pendingOrderId` before the reload that follows an action. That left a gap where the filter re-enabled while the table still showed the old data. Now the order stays pending until the reload finishes; the reset sits in a `finally`, so the controls come back even if the reload fails.

**Checked in the browser:** I slowed POST requests by 1.5s and clicked Start on Elena:
- **Before:** the filter buttons and Refresh were enabled.
- **During:** all of them were disabled.
- **After:** all were enabled again, and Elena's row showed `preparing` with only Ready.

I reseeded the database afterwards and deleted the browser tool's `.playwright-mcp/` folder.

**Nit: `void` removed**
- From the two handlers in `App.tsx`: `() => reload()` and `(orderId, action) => runAction(orderId, action)`.
- From the effect in `useQueue.ts`: now `reload();`.
- The remaining `void`s are return types (`=> void`, `Promise<void>`), not the operator.

The one console error on page load is just the browser requesting `/favicon.ico`, which the app doesn't have. If you want it gone, the simplest fix is an empty inline icon in `index.html`.

I've trimmed the comments and simplified the Sequelize annotations across the API (`web/` untouched). It's a net 194 lines removed against 65 added. All 119 tests still pass, the seed still gives identical results on a rerun, and the test database rebuilds and migrates cleanly.

**Should fix: comments**
- **Removed** comments that only restated a file's layer or role:
  - headers of `modules/orders.js`, `endpoints/orders.js`, `errors.js`, `test/integration/helpers/db.js` and `.sequelizerc`;
  - doc lines that repeated the code, e.g. "Applies an action…", "Sum of prep_time_minutes * quantity…", "Creates an order and its items in one go", and obvious `@param` descriptions.
- **Shortened** comments that explain a reason to one or two lines:
  - **Priority and transitions:** the `priority.js` header (pure function, `now` passed in, UTC ms), the two `promised_at` helpers, the comparator, `rankOrders`, and the `transitions.js` header (one line: legal only if listed in the map).
  - **Repository, endpoints, schema:** the repository header and compare-and-set note, the endpoint error mapping, the models header, migration headers, config, and the Jest and global-setup headers.
  - **Seeder header:** now one line saying it's idempotent with dates relative to now, the expected-scores table, and a single short paragraph covering both tied pairs. I also reordered the table to match the real ranking.
- **Kept** comments that explain why: `priority.js` L81 as you asked, the inclusive buckets with overdue landing in the first, "not floored: 30m30s…", the compare-and-set race in the module, `Sequelize.DATE` being timestamptz, the status index, the UTC timezone, the separate test database, and the express JSON parse error.

**Nit: Sequelize glue annotations**
- **Seeder:**
  - Removed the `SeedOrder` typedef, the `MENU_ITEMS` type, the `addMinutes` JSDoc, the `insertReturning` helper and all nested casts.
  - `bulkInsert` now passes `{ transaction, returning: [...] }` directly.
  - This type-checks because `queryInterface` is untyped (`any`), so the missing `returning` in Sequelize's typings no longer matters.
- **Migrations:** removed the `@type {{ up, down }}` and `@param` blocks.
- **`config.js`:** removed the `DbConfig` typedef and annotations; only a small `'postgres'` constant cast is left.
- **`models/index.js`:** `config[env]` became `NODE_ENV === 'test' ? config.test : config.development`. That avoids indexing an untyped object with a string. It also changes one behaviour: an unknown `NODE_ENV` now falls back to development instead of failing.
- All files keep `// @ts-check`.

**Type-check scope**
- **App code** (modules, repository, endpoints, app, config, models, test helpers) still passes the strict check.
- **Migrations and seeder** pass the editor's default check, which is what runs here since the repo has no `jsconfig.json`. If you add a strict `jsconfig.json` later, these glue files would report implicit-`any` parameters.

I updated my saved note to match: full JSDoc on app code, minimal on Sequelize glue.

content.text:
I added a Vitest test file for `QueueTable` with 8 tests covering your four cases, and they all pass. When I deliberately broke the component in each of the four ways, the matching tests failed. `npm test` now runs the 119 API tests and then these 8, and the web build still passes.

**Dependencies:** added to `web` as dev dependencies:
- `vitest` 5.0.3
- `jsdom` 28.1.0
- `@testing-library/react` 16.3.3, `@testing-library/dom` 10.4.2, `@testing-library/user-event` 14.6.7, `@testing-library/jest-dom` 7.0.1

I used jsdom 28 instead of the latest 30 because 30 requires Node ≥ 22.22.2. With `engine-strict` on, that would make `npm install` fail on earlier Node 22 versions. jsdom 28 supports Node 22.12 and up, the same minimum Vite 8 already needs.

**Setup**
- **`web/vite.config.ts`:** added a `test` section that uses jsdom and a setup file.
- **`web/src/setupTests.ts`:** adds the jest-dom checks such as `toBeDisabled`. It also clears the rendered component after each test, since Testing Library can't do that on its own here.
- **`web/package.json`:** `test` runs `vitest run`, and `test:watch` runs `vitest`.
- **Root `package.json`:** `test` and `test:unit` now also run the web tests, and there's a new `test:web`.

**`QueueTable.test.tsx`**
| Your case | Test | Broken on purpose by |
|---|---|---|
| Keeps the API order | Rows given out of order (scores 20, 75, 55) render in exactly that order | Sorting rows by score inside the component |
| Only allowed actions | `received` shows Start and Cancel, `preparing` only Ready, `ready` only Picked up, `picked_up` no buttons | Always rendering Start and Cancel |
| Correct action sent | Clicking each of the 4 buttons on order 7 calls `onAction(7, action)` exactly once | Always sending `'start'` |
| Disabled during an action | With an order pending, all buttons on every row are disabled; with nothing pending they're enabled | Never disabling the buttons |

The "only allowed actions" test also covers the spec's optional 11.2 case that Cancel appears only on `received` orders. I didn't add an empty-state test because it wasn't in your list; it would be about five lines if you want it.

Nothing is committed. Your own changes to `DECISIONS.md` and `web/src/App.tsx` are untouched.
